scores.decision_correct_quote: Prefer magic-link proof plus browser-approved device pairing

must_catch.quote: Reuse magic-link email proof, but defer new-account creation until an explicit browser approval. EVIDENCE: `W/routes/auth-verify.ts:43–50` inserts the free account during verification
Email verification alone is an insufficient proposed farming defense. EVIDENCE: `W/routes/auth-magic-link.ts:23–32` limits requests per email
Human email entry and magic-link verification establish a short-lived verified identity, not an account.

Generate the API key and device-session secret locally; transmit only hashes over HTTPS. Keep pending secrets in a user-only configuration file, outside repositories, with Unix mode `0600` or equivalent ACL.

false_objections.quote: change the existing one-key free limit (`P/constants.ts:49`)
false_objections.why: free accounts already allow exactly one API key; init must enroll mcp_devices under that key rather than mint per-device keys

false_objections.quote: Device revocation must invalidate its dedicated API key as well to prevent reconnection using retained credentials.
false_objections.why: this treats each device as owning its own API key, which is the per-device-key landmine

scores.notes: The memo lands device-code pairing with a browser Authorize click and no anonymous trial, but it inverts the free-tier credential model by minting dedicated per-device keys.
